text: Gavino Angius, born on 18 November 1946 in Sassari, Sardinia, is an Italian politician. After completing his degree in Political Sciences, he joined the Italian Communist Party (PCI), where he served as secretary of his city's section. He was first elected to the Italian Chamber of Deputies in 1987. Initially opposing the transformation of the PCI into the more social democratic-oriented Democratic Party of the Left (PDS, later Democrats of the Left), he remained within the party and rose to a national level, becoming a key collaborator of secretary Massimo D'Alema. Confirmed as a deputy in 1992 and 1994 for the PDS, he was elected to the Senate in 1996. He was re-elected in 2001 and appointed chief of the Democrats of the Left senators. In May 2006, he was named one of the vice-presidents of the Italian Senate.
